question:
I have a Snowflake share and listing between two accounts in different regions for one table. The share works until the table is rebuilt through scheduled dbt jobs, then the share expectedly loses select privilege on the table.

My solution for this was to add on on run end hook to my dbt project the re-grants the privilege. However after adding the hook, I am getting the error in dbt cloud:

002003 (02000): SQL compilation error: Share '"account_locator.PLATINUM_SNOWFLAKE_SECURE_SHARE_1234"' does not exist or not ? authorized.

Running GRANT SELECT ON TABLE platinum.aggregations.table TO SHARE PLATINUM_SNOWFLAKE_SECURE_SHARE_1234; manually in Snowflake with accountadmin or sa_dbtcloud works to re-grant select privilege to the share.

So in my dbt_project.yml I have:

on-run-end:
  - "{% if target.name | lower == 'prod' %} GRANT SELECT ON TABLE platinum.aggregations.table TO SHARE PLATINUM_SNOWFLAKE_SECURE_SHARE_1234; {% endif %}"`

However when running the dbt cloud job, I get the previously mentioned error. Interestingly, the error includes the account locator code even though that is not supplied in the hook
title: How to use dbt on run end hook for Snowflake share privileges?
answer:
Was able to work out solution via helpful user in dbt slack channel:

  • Create new database role (this role cannot have any future grants in order to work with a share)
  • GRANT DATABASE ROLE <name> TO SHARE <share_name> (need to run this only once)
  • Then in the on run end hook use this instead: - "{% if target.name | lower == 'prod' %} grant select on table <database.schema.table> to database role <name>; {% endif %}"

So you grant select privilege on desired table to the database role (which is already granted to the share) instead of granting the privilege directly to the share. I still do not know why the original method does not work though.
